messages.subject: [R-sig-Epi] R-sig-Epi Digest, Vol 41, Issue 1
messages.body_plain:
Ol? Mirian,

Are you using Poisson models with an offset?  I've never tried this  
with the Epi package so giving us some sample code and sample data  
structure would help.

But if you simply use glm, one way to account for over-dispersion is  
by specifying family=quasipoisson.  It maximizes the quasilikelihood  
rather than the likelihood (don't ask me the maths of this, maybe  
start with the Wikipedia...).

Another approach might be hierarchical modelling but we'd need to know  
your data structure.

Cheers.

David Evans
-----------------
Epidemiologist, Kappa Sant?

messages.subject_clean: Anyone know of a good factors analysis library for R?
messages.body_plain:
Trying to separatey correlate the regions of HIV-1's gp120 
with neutralization data. I have comparison matrixes for 
the sequences and cross-clade neutralization data. My guess
is that analyzing in the individual regions will give us
better correlation with the neutralization data, but at 
this point cannot find a good package for analyzing the 
similarity matrixes. 

The inputs inlcude a square matrixes of comparisons between
each clade for each region and cross-clade antibody responses.

What I need is a level of correlation between the neutralization
data and the similarity matrixes. 

Searching CRAN for "factors analysis", "cross clade", and
"corretion model" in various combinations hadn't gotten me
anything that looks relevant.

Any advice would be appreciated.

thanx

--

messages.body_plain:
Dear Steven,

You find the classical Factor Analysis in
factanal in the package "stats".

FA is found also in other packages.

If you want Confirmative Factor Analysis
you find it as a subset of sem in the "sem" package.

Good luck.

Ralf Finne
Novia University of Applied Sciences.
Finland.

messages.body_plain:
Dear Steven,

There are lots of factor analysis packages in R,  but it sounds from the
below like you want something that can handle sequences too.  Have you tried
looking in Bioconductor:

http://www.bioconductor.org/

Alternately, the genetics and phylogenetics views in CRAN may have what you
want:

http://cran.r-project.org/web/views/Genetics.html

http://cran.r-project.org/web/views/Phylogenetics.html

Best,
Amy

messages.body_plain:
Hi Steven,

I'm a bit hazy on population genetics myself - I was using Bioconductor
packages for analysis of gene expression experiments done on microarrays and
/ or real time PCR.

However, Bioconductor has an extremely helpful and active mailing list, and
I do seem to remember some discussion on it a while ago regarding a package
dealing with a similar situation to yours.  In the first instance, you could
browse through the brief descriptions of the packages:

http://www.bioconductor.org/packages/2.6/bioc/

where you will find a number that are made to analyze sequences, for example
GeneR, GeneRfold, GeneticsPed, cosmo etc.  Click on the name of the package
to see a more detailed description, you can also look at the help files /
manuals / vignettes for each package from there.

If you are still not sure if there is anything that fits your needs, you
could also email the bioconductor mailing group:

http://www.bioconductor.org/docs/mailList.html

Hope it helps,
Best
Amy
